newsitem.title: USA: Sprint reiterates different local strategy.
newsitem.headline: Sprint reiterates different local strategy.

text.p: Long distance telephone company Sprint Corp took a step Monday to innoculate itself against losses suffered by the stock of competitor MCI Communications Corp late last week by reiterating the differences between the companies' plans to enter the local telephone market.

In a statement Monday, Sprint chairman and chief executive officer William Esrey stressed that Sprint's efforts to get into the local market do not involve a heavy up-front capital investment in local facilities.

"Our initial efforts in expansion markets utilizes a resale approach that does not entail a significant up-front investment in local facilities that has been favored by some of our competitors," Esrey said.
On Thursday, MCI said it would incur about twice the losses it originally anticipated as a result of its efforts to enter the local long distance market.
"We wanted to make sure that the market was clear as to what our competitive local strategies were," a Sprint spokesman said of the reason behind Esrey's comments.
MCI fell $7.125 Friday to $35.25 following that company's announcement. Sprint also fell Friday, by 2-3/16 to 49-3/8, in what some viewed as a reaction to the MCI news.
But one analyst said Sprint has repeatedly stressed its lower initial cost local telephone strategy and that the announcement Monday was not new.

"I wouldn't call that announcement market moving," said Barry Sine, analyst at SBC Warburg Inc. "The earnings have been widely known, their strategy has been well articulated. No one would confuse them with MCI."
In his statement, Esrey also said second quarter earnings would be in line with consensus Wall Street estimates.
Sprint shares were up 7/16 at 49-13/16 Monday.
